opening: I went to the pantry in my hall. The fire alarm rang. What happened?

The narrator had planned to go to the pantry to heat up some food for themselves using a cooking appliance kept there. While the food was heating, fats or oils in it gave off smoke; this was ordinary cooking smoke, not an actual fire. The smoke rose and reached a fire alarm located near the pantry, setting it off. So the alarm was a false alarm caused by cooking smoke, and there was no real fire.

The narrator had planned to go to the pantry to cook or heat up food for themselves using a cooking appliance kept there. They deliberately added oil or grease to the appliance (for example, to grease a pan) and overheated it, setting it too high or preheating it too long. When the narrator added the food to the overheated oil, the oil smoked heavily. This cooking smoke rose and reached a fire alarm located near the pantry, causing it to ring. So the narrator's ordinary cooking produced smoke that triggered a false fire alarm, and there was no actual fire.

The narrator went to the pantry intending to cook or heat up food for themselves. The pantry contained both the cooking appliance/pan and the fire alarm. While preparing the food, the narrator added oil and accidentally let it get too hot; the overheated oil began to smoke. Because they were still in the pantry, the smoke rose directly to the fire alarm located in that same pantry, triggering it. There was no real fire — the alarm was a false alarm caused by cooking smoke from overheated oil.

The narrator went to the pantry intending to cook or heat food for themselves. The pantry was equipped with a stove and a pan, and the fire alarm was located in that same pantry. The narrator put oil in the pan and heated it on the stove, then added the food before the alarm rang. The cooking setup accidentally let the oil become overheated — the added oil, rather than the food itself, was the main source of the smoke. That smoke rose directly to the nearby fire alarm in the pantry and set it ringing. There was no actual fire; it was a false alarm caused by cooking smoke in the pantry.

revealed_source_answer:
I cooked food with a very high temperature (without burning the food) in the pantry. However, I forgot to turn on the exhaust fan. Since the smoke detecter in the building is very sensitive, the grease fumes triggered the fire alarm.

Here hall means a residential hall and pantry means its small shared kitchen plus food storage. The narrator enters before starting to cook, rather than fetching an ingredient from another room. The pan is initially empty before oil and food are added. Both the smoke detector and alarm are inside the pantry.
